## Simple explanation

Supervised learning uses examples that include the desired answer. A model
learns from input-label pairs and then predicts labels or values for new
inputs.

## Technical explanation

Given labeled examples $(x_i,y_i)$, supervised learning selects a model
from a hypothesis class by minimizing a training objective and possibly
regularization. Classification predicts discrete labels; regression
predicts numeric targets. Generalization is assessed on data excluded from
fitting.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Supervised learning is widely used for prediction when labeled examples
are available. Label quality, representativeness, leakage prevention, and
deployment distribution strongly influence model usefulness.

## How it works

The data is split into training and evaluation sets. A learning algorithm
fits parameters to minimize loss on training examples; model selection
uses validation data, and final performance is measured on a separate test
set or suitable deployment evaluation.

## Practical example

A maintenance system can learn from historical sensor readings labeled
with whether equipment failed within a defined period. The target window
and data cutoff must be chosen so training examples do not include
information from the future.

## Common misconceptions

- More labeled data does not fix inconsistent labels or a mismatch with
  deployment conditions.
- High training performance does not establish that the model generalizes
  to new data.
